thread:
dan: Quick follow-up to the gateway streaming/retries RFC — can we nail down the concrete semantics for retries vs resume tokens? I sketched a couple options but want engineering tradeoffs before we lock anything in.

tess: Agree we should pick a simple surface that covers 90%. My proposal:
- Gateway MAY perform 1 automatic retry for non-streaming, idempotent requests (has `Idempotency-Key` or safe method) if the backend failed before any response bytes were written.
- For streaming (chunked/SSE/grpc-stream) do NOT auto-retry. Instead support a lightweight resume token that lets clients reconnect and continue from last-acked chunk.

ravi: Stateful resume is the big cost here. Storing full KV cache per request will explode mem. Two possible approaches:
1) Minimal server-side resume: store only (offset, small metadata, backend session id) in redis with TTL (e.g. 2m). Token = opaque id that maps to redis entry. Pros: small tokens, easy revoke. Cons: requires infra and cross-region consistency if gateway != runtime.
2) Stateless resume: token carries base64-encoded prefix digest + resume offset so runtime can rehydrate from prefix cache. Pros: no central store. Cons: token size and security concerns.

mike: Operational concern — Dedicated/Private installs may not want gateway to carry resume state. I think ownership should be pushed towards the runtime: gateway just proxies stream and detects errors, but for resume it returns a standardized `X-Resume-Required: true` + info about how to contact runtime or an ephemeral endpoint. That keeps gateway lightweight.

tess: To reconcile: make the resume flow pluggable.
- Default: Gateway-managed resume (redis TTL) for hosted offering — lower client complexity.
- Opt-out: For Dedicated/Private, runtime-managed resume (gateway returns resume challenge pointing at runtime) or client does manual reconnect.

mike: Also: automatic retry rules (proposal):
- If backend connection fails before first byte -> gateway can retry transparently once to another healthy backend.
- If any response bytes sent -> gateway MUST NOT retry; instead return `206`/`202` with resume info or close connection plainly.

dan: Example of resume headers I'm imagining:
```
Request:  POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  X-Request-Id: 01FZ...
  Idempotency-Key: <uuid>

Response (on transient failure while streaming):
  HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
  X-Resume-Token: r=eyJzZXNzaW9uIjo... (opaque)
  X-Resume-TTL: 120
```
Client can then re-POST with `X-Resume-Token` to continue.

ravi: TTL and size caps matter. Suggest defaults: TTL=120s, max stored metadata 8KB, max token lifespan 10m if explicitly requested. Also need encryption/HMAC for tokens so customers can't tamper.

tess: We also need to define metrics/tracing hooks: `gateway.resume.created`, `gateway.resume.resumed`, `gateway.retry.attempt`, `gateway.retry.success`, and tag them with route/model and `bytes_streamed_before_failure`.

mike: One more: backpressure. If gateway is doing batching across requests, resume semantics must capture KV-cache index for that backend so replays don't re-run expensive computation or violate cache assumptions. That suggests runtime-provided resume metadata is more accurate.

dan: Tradeoffs summary I posted in the RFC draft earlier, but to be explicit here:
- Gateway-managed resume: simpler for clients, more infra state, easier to route/failover.
- Runtime-managed resume: places complexity in runtime, better for Dedicated/Private, fewer cross-region concerns.
- No-resume + 0-retry: simplest, but poor UX for flaky networks during long streams.

tess: Action items:
1) I'll update the RFC with pluggable resume ownership and default TTL/size constraints.
2) @mike can you enumerate integration checklist for Dedicated/Private (runtime endpoints + docs)?
3) @ravi please draft a minimal redis schema and HMAC scheme for tokens.

mike: Will do, adding a note about config toggles for `resume.store=gateway|runtime|none` and a runtime handshake protocol for resume endpoints.

infra-bot: deploybot: RFC branch `edge/retry-resume` updated -> https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/edge/retry-resume

dan: Awesome. One last point — observability: include example logs for a resume event so SRE can alert on high resume rates (possible backend instability).

tess: +1 :thumbsup: 

ravi: minor nit: define error codes for client so SDKs can surface: `RESUME_UNSUPPORTED`, `RESUME_EXPIRED`, `RESUME_REJECTED`.

dan: Perfect. If no blockers I'll merge the RFC changes by EOD and open a follow-up PR for the gateway config flags.

mike: no blockers from infra side.
